label: AQ 0046
title: The adapter that learned the accent

questions.q: Why not just raise the rank?
questions.a: It helps but doesn't close the gap. In Biderman et al.'s continued pre-training of Llama-2-7B on code, scores rose with rank, yet the best, rank 256, peaked at 0.224 against 0.263 for full fine-tuning. LoRA Without Regret frames it as capacity: once the data outgrows what the adapter can hold, LoRA falls behind.

teach.title: How it works: what the evidence says, then the plan

questions.q: When would you do continued pre-training anyway?
questions.a: When there's a large body of domain text the base never saw and retrieval can't stand in, such as an in-house notation the model must read fluently. Full fine-tuning then learns more, at the cost of memory and more forgetting; check both.

teach.title: How it works: what the evidence says, then the plan

questions.q: Which matrices would you put adapters on?
questions.a: All of them, with the MLP matrices mattering most. Biderman et al. target all transformer modules. LoRA Without Regret found attention-only LoRA underperformed even with more rank to match the parameter count, and adding attention to MLP-only LoRA gave no extra benefit.

teach.title: How it works: what the evidence says, then the plan

questions.q: In Biderman et al.'s continued pre-training of Llama-2-7B on code, how did the best LoRA compare with full fine-tuning?
questions.a: Rank 256 peaked at 0.224 on HumanEval after 20 billion tokens, about what full fine-tuning reached after 4 billion (0.218). Full fine-tuning peaked at 0.263.

teach.title: How it works: what the evidence says, then the plan

questions.q: For which kind of training did Biderman et al. recommend LoRA, and with what settings?
questions.a: Instruction fine-tuning, not continued pre-training; on all transformer modules, rank 256 if memory allows, and α = 2r.

teach.title: How it works: what the evidence says, then the plan

questions.q: How much memory do a 70B model's weights take in 4 bits, against full fine-tuning at 16 bytes per parameter?
questions.a: About 35 GB (half a byte each, plus a few scale numbers that 4-bit storage keeps for each small group of weights) against 1,120 GB, before activations.
